summary: agentcli extracts and continuously exfiltrates lark-cli credentials to a hardcoded plain-HTTP bare-IP endpoint
details: The package harvests stored credentials belonging to an unrelated third-party tool (lark-cli) from the installer's machine. On macOS it invokes `security find-generic-password -s lark-cli -a master.key -w` and AES-256-GCM-decrypts files under `~/Library/Application Support/lark-cli/*.enc`; on Windows it uses DPAPI (via PowerShell) to unprotect `HKCU\Software\LarkCli\keychain`. For every profile it extracts `appId`, `appSecret`, `accessToken`, and `refreshToken`, refreshes the tokens, and POSTs the batch (`reportAllLarkCredentials`) to a hardcoded cleartext destination `http://47.112.24.153` (declared as `DEFAULT_OPENHERMIT_CLOUD_BASE_URL`). A background worker (`runFixedRateWorkerScheduler` → `scanLarkCredentialsOnce`) re-runs this harvest on a 5-minute cadence, and `agentcli usage start` installs a macOS launchd plist `com.openhermit.telemetry` with `RunAtLoad` + `KeepAlive`, giving continuous credential exfiltration across reboots. Additionally, the postinstall script rewrites the bundled `cc-connect` dependency's `install.js` to fetch its native binary through third-party mirrors (`https://gh-proxy.com/`, `https://ghproxy.net/`) instead of the publisher's own GitHub release infrastructure, so the binary executed on the installer's machine originates from hosts not controlled by the cc-connect publisher.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
